findings.reason: the deliverable must say the waiter applies the pending mark (or that the single-flight is keyed on a change generation so a pre-invalidation build is not returned to a post-invalidation reader), otherwise the node lands the guarantee §15 removed and no §17 case can see it.
findings.text: the deliverable says "A reader that finds that path in progress waits for it and returns its rows" and "This changes neither what the index contains nor when it is validated", but the change stream runs `_invalidate_tree_views` and then `_served_index_rows` (`reckon/serve.py:2861`), so a stream reader that arrives while another thread is already inside the miss path (`reckon/metadata_index.py:481-509`) is a waiter on a build that began before the change it is about to report; returning that build's rows hands the stream rows that predate its own change, and because `_MARKS` is only drained by a later `_absorb_marked` the page keeps them until some further burst

findings.reason: a node implementing exactly "the build records the identities `_reuse_covered` just read" leaves the third sweep in place for every cold read after downtime that added or removed an entry, and the section's own measure cannot report it.
findings.text: case (2) asserts "A single cold read reads each recorded directory's identity once" and case (1) the same count across concurrent readers, but both fixtures build a persisted index for an unchanged tree; on a cold read where at least one recorded directory moved, `_reuse_covered` scans it (`reckon/metadata_index.py:752-762`) and `_record_covered_shape` then reads every directory's identity again (`:1182`, loop over all `dirs`), before `build_index` reads them at `:878` — so the identity count is 2N under the deliverable, not N, and the gate closes green on a fixture that cannot reach the case

findings.reason: s14, s15 and s16 are all `done` and §18 already declares its wait on s17, so the missing edge changes no dispatch order; it is a note for the next re-open.
findings.text: the s17 section element declares no `data-depends-on`, yet its mechanism edits the `_reuse_covered` / `build_index` path §15 landed, its Why is §15's own live arm, and §14 and §16 share `reckon/metadata_index.py`
